title: Go SDK: typed response structs, generics helpers, and robust structured-output decoding
creator: Maya Patel
description: Add first-class typed response structs and a small set of generics-based helpers to make streaming decoding, retries, and structured-output parsing ergonomic and safe for Go users. Goal: reduce boilerplate in customer code, provide canonical examples for decoding model-generated JSON into typed structs, and expose composable retry/backoff behaviors for streaming and non-streaming calls.
acceptance_criteria: Define canonical typed response structs for common API shapes (Completion, ChatMessage, Embedding) with JSON tags and validation helpers.
Implement a lightweight generics-based DecodeStream[T any] helper that consumes SDK stream and emits typed objects via channel, honoring ctx cancellation.
Provide DecodeStructuredOutput helper that attempts JSON decode, then schema-validate (optional), with clear error types for partial parse vs. validation failures.
Expose retry wrappers that work with streaming (resume semantics where possible) and non-streaming calls, with test coverage for backoff jitter and idempotency decisions.
Add three runnable examples in examples/go/ showing: simple typed decode, streaming decode with cancellation, and structured output + schema validation example.
Document behavioral guarantees in SDK docs and include migration notes for existing Go customers.
Ship behind feature flag sdk-go-typed-output and add telemetry event for decode errors first 30 days.
Unit and integration tests reaching >=80% coverage on new helpers and examples.
Code reviewed by runtime and SDK teams and merged to release branch sdk-go-1.6.
Updated changelog and a short note in the SDK migration guide.

notes: Trade-off: We prefer explicit typed structs over reflect-based dynamic maps to catch schema changes at compile time; this increases maintenance when API shapes evolve.
Backwards compatibility: helpers are additive and behind feature flag; existing decoding APIs remain untouched.
Performance: initial microbenchmarks show ~5-8% overhead vs manual json.Decoder for tiny payloads, acceptable given ergonomics gains. Will revisit after broader e2e benchmarking.
